/PubMed + Unpaywall), and a Web sidebar layout fix.
# dsh-plugins
Four plugins for DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`).
| Plugin | Category | What it does |
| dsh-scholar | tools | Four model-facing tools for literature work — `paper_search`, `paper_get`, `
paper_citations`, `book_search` — over OpenAlex, arXiv, Crossref, Semantic Scholar and PubMed, with

open-access PDF resolution through Unpaywall |
| dsh-sidebar-tidy | ui | Keeps the Web sidebar works
pace and session list clickable when footer plugins grow tall, by capping and scrolling the plugin-a

ction area |
| dsh-karing | tools | The same for a local Karing installation, but with **eight** too
ls and a different split-tunnel model: Karing keeps three mixed inbounds alive, so switching modes j
ust repoints the system proxy at another port — under a second, and the core is never restarted. Als
o embeds the kernel into the plugin, self-manages the node subscription, and ships a rate-limit / se

ssion / anti-bot layer for the search engines it scrapes |
| dsh-corpus | tools | Full-text search o
ver a document corpus: a bigram inverted index with simplified↔traditional folding, so **two-charact
er** Chinese queries work (SQLite FTS5 `trigram` needs three and returns nothing for 紫微 or 用神), plus
a metadata-vs-content split so index files do not drown out real documents |

Each is a Cordis plugin that declares a `dsh.bundle` manifest, so it installs with
`dsh plugin add`.

## Requirements
DSH 0.1.0-rc.1 or newer, and Node 20+.

The plugins import `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` and `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`
dynamically and degrade g

racefully when they are absent, which is why both are
declared as *optional* peers — installing thes

e plugins never pulls official
packages into your profile.

`dsh-karing` is **Windows only** and expects Karing to be installed already. It
can either drive the

copy you installed, or embed a copy of `karingService.exe`
into `<plugin>/runtime/` via `tools/embe

d-kernel.mjs` — which is what lets it run
**alongside** the Karing GUI instead of fighting it for po

— which is what lets it run
**alongside** the Karing GUI instead of fighting it for ports 3065–3067.

Nothing in this repository ships Karing's binaries. `runtime/` and `data/` are
git-ignored: the kern

el copy, the search index and the runtime state are all
generated locally.
